entries.excerpt_for_model: Our Clients: Field Level Media - Professional sports content solutions | FLM NFL NCAAF MLB NHL NBA Golf ODDS Football NFL NCAAF UFL Basketball NBA NCAAB WNCAAB WNBA Esports Golf PGA Tour LPGA Tour LIV DP World Tour Champions Tour Soccer MLS WORLD CUP World Cup (W) Friendly NWSL EPL Premier Baseball MLB NCAA Hockey NHL PWHL Auto Racing NASCAR Formula 1 Indy Car Fighting UFC Boxing Tennis ATP Tour WTA Olympics Olympics Other About us Products / Services Contact us Privacy Policy NFL NCAAF MLB NHL NBA Golf ODDS Football NFL NCAAF UFL Basketball NBA NCAAB WNCAAB WNBA Esports Golf PGA Tour LPGA Tour LIV DP World Tour Champions Tour Soccer MLS WORLD CUP World Cup (W) Friendly NWSL EPL Premier Baseball MLB NCAA Hockey NHL PWHL Auto Racing NASCAR Formula 1 Indy Car Fighting UFC Boxing Tennis ATP Tour WTA Olympics Olympics Other Home > Villanova, Notre Dame set to kick off college basketball season in Rome Basketball NCAAB News Preview Story Oct 20, 2026 3:39 am Villanova, Notre Dame set to kick off college basketball season in Rome Photo by: Wendell Cruz / Imagn Images The 2026-27 college basketball season opener will enjoy a unique backdrop, as Notre Dame and Villanova will send their teams to Rome to tip off on Nov. 1. The men’s teams will play that Sunday morning U.S. time, followed by a game between their women’s teams. Pope Leo XIV — the first American-born pope and a Villanova graduate — was invited to attend, and the players were scheduled to have an audience with him before the games, though those plans are less certain following news that Leo required surgery to remove a cancerous nodule from his lung. The trip will also be an early homecoming for Luigi Suigo, the 7-foot-3 Italian center who joined Villanova after playing for clubs in Milan and Belgrade, Serbia. Still 19, Suigo is adjusting to the American game and recently committed two fouls in the first 76 seconds of an exhibition game against George Mason. “He’s got to learn,” Wildcats coach Kevin Willard said. “… I think everyone sees a 7-foot-3 kid and automatically thinks he’s a grown man. A 19-year-old from Italy who has never played high-major basketball, he has to figure it out a little bit, and we have to be patient with him and you have to go through some growing pains a little bit.” Villanova expects to be firmly in the Big East title chase. Voted third in the preseason coaches’ poll behind only UConn and St. John’s, the Wildcats return Tyler Perkins, a preseason all-conference first-teamer who led them last season with 13.7 points per game. They added transfer forwards Kwame Evans Jr. (Oregon) and Devin Royal (Ohio State). Perkins, Royal and Suigo were the only players in the starting lineups for each of Villanova’s first two exhibitions. Evans is day-to-day with a left leg injury. “I didn’t have to watch film of (Royal or Evans) because I had seen so much of (them) live,” Willard said. “I respected them from having gone up against them. … I’m still trying to figure out everybody.”

CBS Sports college basketball insider Jon Rothstein reported Tuesday that senior guard Tyler Perkins has been fully cleared for all basketball activities following offseason surgery on his right shoulder. Perkins underwent arthroscopic surgery in late April and was cleared for everything except contact work as recently as August. Now, with Villanova set to open its season against Notre Dame in Rome on Nov. 1, that restriction is officially gonezo. Pretty good timing. Perkins is one of only three returning rotation players from Kevin Willard’s first Nova team, and easily the most important of the bunch. He averaged 13.7 points and 5.4 rebounds last season, won Big East Most Improved Player, and now enters his senior year as a preseason All-Big East First Team selection, according to Rothstein. He’s also projected to start alongside Elijah Crawford, Devin Royal, Kwame Evans Jr. and Luigi Suigo on a Wildcats team Rothstein ranked No. 28 entering the season. Unfortunately, the update on Matt Hodge wasn’t quite as encouraging (but was also expected). Rothstein reported that the redshirt sophomore forward “continues to progress” from the torn ACL he suffered against St. John’s in February, but there remains no timetable for his return. Hodge underwent surgery shortly after the injury, so missing the Nov. 1 opener wouldn’t exactly be surprising. A return around the beginning of Big East play in December would put him roughly 10 months removed from the injury, but without an official timetable, there’s no point in me trying to play detective yet. Willard at least has a ton more depth to work with this season than compared to last. Rothstein projects Hodge as part of a bench that also includes four-star freshman Adam Oumiddoch, Jake Fiegen, and Buddy Simmons, giving Nova plenty of options while he works his way back.
